content.text:
I found one code in the knowledge store that specifically identifies eosinophilic oesophagitis.

**Codelist**

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| J1017 | Eosinophilic oesophagitis |

**Codes I left out**

These came up in the search but don't specifically indicate the condition:
- **General oesophagitis codes:** J101 Oesophagitis, J101y Other specified oesophagitis and J101z Oesophagitis NOS. These cover any cause of oesophagitis, not just the eosinophilic type.
- **Other types of oesophagitis:** reflux or peptic (J1011 and its synonyms), chemical (J1012), postoperative (J1013), ulcerative (J1016) and others. These are different conditions.
- **General eosinophil codes:** D403 Eosinophilic disorder, D4033 Allergic eosinophilia, and eosinophil count results (42K…). None of these is specific to the oesophagus.
- **Other allergic gut conditions:** for example J4320 Allergic gastroenteritis and J1540 Allergic gastritis. These affect other parts of the gut.
- **Possible signs or complications:** oesophageal stricture or rings (J103…, J1033) and food stuck in the oesophagus (TF13). These can happen with eosinophilic oesophagitis but don't show that someone has it.

Because only one code is specific, anyone recorded with a broader code such as "Oesophagitis NOS" won't be picked up. If you'd rather catch more possible cases, even at the cost of some wrong ones, you could add J101z or J101y.

content.text:
I found one code that specifically means eosinophilic oesophagitis:

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| **J1017** | Eosinophilic oesophagitis |

I searched the knowledge store for "eosinophilic esophagitis/oesophagitis" and "allergic eosinophilic oesophagitis" and found no other codes, synonyms or subtypes for this condition.

**Codes I left out**, because none of them shows the person has eosinophilic oesophagitis:
- **General oesophagitis codes** (J101 Oesophagitis, J101y Other specified oesophagitis, J101z Oesophagitis NOS). These cover any kind of oesophagitis.
- **Other types of oesophagitis**, such as reflux, peptic, chemical or ulcerative oesophagitis.
- **General eosinophilic disorders** (D403 Eosinophilic disorder, D4033 Allergic eosinophilia, D4035 Hypereosinophilic syndrome). These are body-wide or blood conditions, not specific to the oesophagus.
- **Allergic gut conditions in other places** (J4320 Allergic gastroenteritis, J1540 Allergic gastritis, J4323 Allergic colitis).
- **Eosinophil blood test results** (42K and related codes). These are lab results, not a diagnosis.

Because this list has only one code, it may miss some cases. People with the condition might be recorded under J101y or J101z instead. Adding those would catch more cases but also pull in people with other kinds of oesophagitis.

content.text:
I found one code in the knowledge store that specifically records eosinophilic esophagitis:

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| **J1017** | Eosinophilic oesophagitis |

I searched for "eosinophilic esophagitis", "eosinophilic oesophagitis" and "allergic esophagitis". The store has no other codes for this condition, including no extra spellings or child codes under J1017.

**Codes I left out:**
- **Too general:** Oesophagitis (J101), Oesophagitis NOS (J101z), Other specified oesophagitis (J101y), Eosinophilic disorder (D403) and Allergic eosinophilia (D4033). These cover eosinophilic esophagitis, but they mostly capture other conditions, so they would bring in many people who don't have it.
- **Different oesophagitis types:** reflux, peptic, ulcerative, chemical, postoperative, phlegmonous and gangrenous oesophagitis.
- **Possible complications or related findings:** oesophageal stricture and Lower oesophageal mucosal ring (J1033). These don't confirm the condition on their own.
- **Other conditions:** Allergic gastroenteritis/colitis (J432 group), food allergy codes, eosinophil count tests, and eosinophilic disorders at other body sites.

Because there is only one code, this codelist will probably miss some patients. People with eosinophilic esophagitis may be recorded under general oesophagitis codes, especially in older records. If you'd rather catch more cases and accept some wrong ones, you could add J101z or J101y.
